simple.meaning: מְנָא (mᵉnâʼ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to count , appoint.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 7:25. Its contexts include Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְנָא (H4483).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מְנָא (mᵉnâʼ) / H4483 is traced through Ezra 7:25, Daniel 2:24, Daniel 2:49, Daniel 3:12 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4483. mena or menah מְנָה verb number, reckon (see Biblical Hebrew); — Pe`al Perfect 3masculine singular ׳מ Dan 5:26 God has numbered (the days of) thy kingdom (accusative; i.e. put an end to it); — מְנֵא see below Pa`el appoint , accusative of person: Perfect 3masculine singular מַנִּי Dan 2:24 (+ Infinitive), 2:49 ( ל person + עַל of thing); 2 masculine singular מִבִּיתָ 3:12 ( עַל of thing); Imperative masculine singular מֶנִּי (K §, 47, 3 , c )) Ezra 7:25 .

occurrences.englishText: You, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges, who may judge all the people who are beyond the River, who all know the laws of your God; and teach him who doesn’t know them.

Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said this to him: “Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will show to the king the interpretation.”
Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon; but Daniel was in the king’s gate.

There are certain Jews whom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, O king, have not respected you. They don’t serve your gods, and don’t worship the golden image which you have set up.”
